chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from al-Nakha'i, Abu al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A man forgot the sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah. He said: He must repeat the sa'y. I said: What if he has departed? He said: He must return and repeat the sa'y. This is not like the throwing of the jamarat; indeed, the throwing is a sunnah, while the sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah is an obligation. And he said regarding a man who deliberately abandoned the sa'y: He has no hajj.

key_terms.السَّعْيَ: the ritual walking between al-Safa and al-Marwah during hajj
key_terms.الصَّفَا: al-Safa, one of the two well-known points of sa'y
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwah, the other point of sa'y
key_terms.حَجَّ: the pilgrimage rite whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.رَمْيِ الْجِمَارِ: the throwing of the pebbles at the jamarat during hajj rites
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: a prescribed sunnah act, not at the level of an essential obligation here
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٌ: an obligatory duty whose omission invalidates the rite in this context

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone forgets or deliberately leaves the sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah during hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith states that sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah is a mandatory part of hajj and must be performed even if a person has already left and must return. It also distinguishes sa'y from the throwing of the jamarat, describing the latter as sunnah and the former as a faridah, and rules that one who intentionally abandons sa'y has no valid hajj.
